title: Resume vs LinkedIn Profile: How They Differ and What to Hire For
h1: Resume vs LinkedIn profile: how they differ and what to hire for
description: How a resume and a LinkedIn profile differ in purpose, tone, length and audience, how to keep them consistent and which writing services fit your job search.
intro: Job seekers often treat their LinkedIn profile as an online copy of their resume. The two overlap, but they do different jobs. A resume is a targeted document sent for a specific role, while a profile is a public, searchable page that recruiters find on their own. Understanding the difference helps you decide whether to hire a resume writer, a profile writer or both, and what to ask each for.

faq.q: Should my resume and profile say the same thing?
faq.a: They should agree on facts like dates and titles, but the profile can be broader and more personal.

faq.q: Do I need a designed resume?
faq.a: For many roles a clean, simple layout works best, especially when applications go through screening software.
Yes. Many writers offer packages that include a resume, cover letter and profile.

faq.q: How long should a resume be?
faq.a: Often one to two pages, depending on experience and the conventions in your country and field.

faq.q: Should I write in first person on my profile?
faq.a: Many people do. It feels natural in the summary section, while resumes usually avoid pronouns.
